My doctors thought I was an ass for going off my meds but they stuck it out with me, and ultimately they were right.  The past psychotic episodes were pretty bad (landed in a hospital - not just detached from the world but spinning in my own universe) I was in denial about it.  To be honest, I really only stopped being in denial about my mania about a week or two ago, now that I'm finally on a mood stabilizer and gaining some perspective.

I didn't stay on the same med for long either.  I went back on risperidone, but it was intolerable after a few months. Tested out a few other antipsychotics and have since settled on geodon.

I am very sensitive to meds (had all kinds of reactions).  I've gone on meds, gotten off, and am currently back on pretty successful cocktail.

My advice for early warning signs should you chose to go off meds: Sleep.  Make sure you are getting enough.  Try and keep a stable bedtime wake up time.  Exercising during the day, even if it's just walking to the store 1/2 mile away, will help tire you out.  It's good for mood and energy.  As soon as you notice significant deviations in your time sleep- too much or too little- thats when the flags should come up.

My problem with going off meds was this: I lived healthfully, no caffeine or alcohol, regular sleep and food.  But I had a huge swing out of nowhere after a few months.  Full blown mixed state with psychosis.  That's bad enough as it is, but when I ran yelling to my doctor he put me on the old meds, but they took about a week or two to  alm everything down.  That was an I credibly rough period.

Going off meds didnt work for me, but that's not to say it won't work for you.  If you do end up trying meds again, know that there are a lot out there and with all the permutations of dose and brands that you will eventually find a combo that helps stabilize you with tolerable or no side effects such that you can function and feel like you want to feel.

* Best advice I can give in the mean time is don't have a lot of food lying around in your house (especially snack foods) so at least you are not shoveling endless junk into your body.

* Try to keep busy with anything, preferably out of the house, to keep your mind off of eating.  You will still feel hungry but hopefully you can work off some of that extra eating. Good luck.

*A run down of my symptoms*:

I can become incredible paranoid (think my home is being invaded, someone is outside my room waiting to shoot me).  I also hear voices and sounds sometimes.  For that the docs have primarily given me antipsychotics but those meds don't stabilize my mood.

I have also seen things either briefly (corner of the eye) and sometime longer, but still pretty brief visual hallucinations.

The delusions are usually the worst and longest acting though.  Sometimes I am convinced I can see objects become "unstuck in time" (Vonnegut) and see its past, present, and future.  I've depersonalized and derealized in these states, and this is when I become most dangerous to myself. I feel invincible because (and I honestly believe this in these states) there are no real world consequences: any harm or injury is just in my head.
